t: Hong Xiuquan, a Hakka who had failed the imperial examinations, came to believe from visions and Christian pamphlets that he was the younger brother of Jesus Christ, sent to rid the world of demons, among them the Qing.

From Nanjing, renamed Tianjing, the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom ruled nearly 30 million people at its peak and announced radical reforms: strict separation of the sexes, the abolition of foot binding, land socialisation and a ban on opium.
Fought as a total war with extreme brutality on both sides, it was the deadliest civil war in history: the most widely cited estimates give 20 to 30 million dead, others as many as 100 million.
dyk: Hong Xiuquan had studied the Bible in Guangzhou with the American Baptist missionary Issachar Jacox Roberts, who refused to baptise him; in 1861 Roberts came to Nanjing, and Hong made him his director of foreign affairs.
ev: Hong Huoxiu fails the imperial examination for the third time and has the visions in which he is given the name Hong Xiuquan
Hong’s follower Feng Yunshan founds the God Worshipping Society in Guangxi
After routing Qing forces at Jintian, Hong declares himself Heavenly King of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom
The Taipings capture Nanjing, rename it Tianjing and kill its Manchu population
In the Tianjing Incident Yang Xiuqing and his followers are slaughtered on Hong Xiuquan’s orders
Zeng Guofan’s Xiang Army captures Anqing, helped by a Royal Navy blockade
Hong Xiuquan dies during the siege, and Nanjing falls to the imperial armies in the Third Battle of Nanjing
The last Taiping army, led by Li Fuzhong, is wiped out on the borders of Hunan, Guizhou and Guangxi

f.where: Southern and central China: Guangxi, where it began at Jintian; Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi and Anhui along the Yangtze; Nanjing, its capital as Tianjing; southern Jiangsu and Zhejiang, the wealthiest region of the empire; with remnants in Fujian, Guangdong, Sichuan and on the Sino-Vietnamese border.
f.period: The God Worshipping Society from 1844; the Jintian uprising, 1850–1851; the march north and down the Yangtze, 1851–1853; the Heavenly Kingdom at Nanjing, 1853–1864, with the failed Northern Expedition and the Tianjing Incident of 1856; the siege and fall of Nanjing, 1862–1864; the last Taiping forces, defeated in 1866 and 1871.
f.figures: Hong Xiuquan, the Heavenly King; Feng Yunshan, founder of the God Worshipping Society; Yang Xiuqing, who claimed to speak as God the Father; Xiao Chaogui; Wei Changhui; Shi Dakai; Hong Rengan, Hong’s cousin; Li Xiucheng, the Loyal King; against them Zeng Guofan of the Xiang Army, Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang.
f.outcome: The Heavenly Kingdom destroyed with the fall of Nanjing in July 1864, in a war whose dead are most widely estimated at 20 to 30 million; a Qing dynasty weakened in central China and forced to rely on Han gentry and their provincial armies; the Self-Strengthening Movement.
